dm.summary:
I started with 'look' and did not reload. My desk was current: all four players' rolls (Ada's Focus 2, a failure; Bram's Move 4; Dev's Sense 6; Cass's Sway 4) were in the tray and the Activity Log, along with Dev's photograph line, the seal, The Lantern Wall and the 03:59 dispatch. The circle shows as finalized and no relationship proposals are waiting for me.

I dealt Ada a Brain mark (From an enemy) from her sheet. It landed at once: the log says 'dealt Ada Quill a Brain mark (1 of 3)' and her roster card now shows 'Marks: 1 Brain'. Bram has Behind Me, so his desk may have offered to take the mark for about two minutes. Nothing on my side shows that offer, so I logged it as F069.

I raised tension to 1 of 4. The open roll on 3 dice came up 2 (Failure), so the mud failed to take Nell. The secret roll on 2 dice came up 6 (Success): the choir below now knows the circle is listening. I sent Ada a private pass note about a voice in the bells that sang the name only her mother used. Then I updated and re-sent the Template dispatch (04:06) to the choirmaster's lodging, one floor below the circle's own loft above the chandler's on Wick Lane.

At the table (#32-37) I answered each roll in the story, set scene 2 and asked each player for one roll. Afterwards I set the pass note recipient back to @Circle and unticked Secret.

There were no console errors. I logged four findings:
- F066: the hourglass has no visible number, tension 0 and 1 look almost the same, and sand already falls at 0.
- F067: praise for how fast and clear the Lightkeeper's bookkeeping is.
- F068: the pass note recipient stays on the last private choice after Send.
- F069: the Lightkeeper is not told when an ally is offered Behind Me.

Small nit, not logged: a screen reader hears 'Secret : only you saw this', with a stray space before the colon. I updated my memory file.

prompts.ada: Scene 2: study the hymn sheet 'For the Low Water' where the handwriting changes halfway down, and work out what the lower hand is really writing. Roll Read (Cunning; Read 2, gilded) on your desk's dice tray and say what you do at the table. Also read your private pass note.
prompts.bram: Scene 2: stand at the window of Mr Abel's lodging and watch both the lane and the room; something keeps moving at the edge of your eye. Roll Survey (Intuition; Survey 2) and say what you do. If your desk offers Behind Me for someone's mark, the choice is yours.
prompts.cass: Scene 2: pick the salt-crusted lock of the tall music cabinet without snapping a pick. Roll Control (Nerve; Control 1) and say what you do; spend Nerve if you like.
prompts.dev: Scene 2: make sense of the choirmaster's daybook on the desk, written in old notation and older symbols. Roll Focus (Intuition; Focus 1, gilded) and say what you do; your grandmother's next verse may be in it.

dm.story_so_far: The Lantern Wall went out to Saltmere's flats at dusk on the lowest tide. Bram found a firm line out to the warm bell rope and pulled up a scrap of choir-white surplice. Ada found that the last bootprint points back toward the shore; the bells got into her head (a Brain mark), and she alone heard a voice sing the name only her mother used. Cass got the mudlark girl Nell talking. When the mud heaved under Nell, the circle pulled her free, and she pointed them to the dead choirmaster Mr Abel's rooms on Wick Lane, humming since Tuesday. Dev heard that the choir sings under the whole shore, strongest beneath the slipway, and that the verse his grandmother hummed is the one the choir has not reached yet; the rope jerked a foot into the mud, and tension rose to 1 of 4. Scene 2 has begun: Mr Abel's lodging, one floor beneath the circle's own loft above the chandler's. In it are a hymn sheet whose handwriting changes halfway down, a salt-crusted locked music cabinet, a daybook in old notation, and humming that the harmonium in the loft above answers.
